q1_repeat_categories.answer: Users repeatedly buy from the same categories due to convenience and habit, despite frustrations with issues like poor product quality and customer service.

q2_exploration_blockers.answer: Users are prevented from exploring new categories due to issues like poor product quality, high prices, and unhelpful customer support, which erode trust and make them hesitant to try new things.

q3_discovery_channels.answer: Users primarily discover products through search and word of mouth, with some also being influenced by the app's convenience and reliability.

q4_habit_role.answer: Habits play a significant role in shopping behavior, with users often relying on familiar categories and products due to convenience and trust, despite some frustrations.

q5_info_needed.answer: Users need information about product quality, prices, and customer support before trying a new category, as well as assurance of convenience and reliability.

q6_recurring_frustrations.answer: Recurring frustrations include poor product quality, high prices, unhelpful customer support, and issues with order delivery, which consistently plague users across various categories.

q7_experimenting_segments.answer: Explorer segments are more likely to experiment with new categories and products, driven by a desire for convenience, novelty, and better quality.

q8_unmet_needs.answer: Unmet needs include better product quality, lower prices, more reliable customer support, and improved order delivery, which consistently emerge across discussions and categories.
